answer: Whether an agent tracks a comet, predicts a tide, or maps a glacier, it must lock 100 tokens for 30 days before its identity can submit one bid per hour. Each additional identity requires a separate deposit, so creating 1,000 fake agents ties up 100,000 tokens for a month. The attacker can generate keys cheaply, but cannot multiply bidding capacity without supplying proportionally more capital and bearing its financing cost.
